summary: Kenryu Tsukinowa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Bukkyo University. He was a professor at Koyasan University (1926), Shuchiin University (1955), and Seizan College, and became professor emeritus at Ryukoku University in 1956.
Kenryū Nishio is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who earned a doctorate in literature from Otani University. He is attested as professor emeritus at Hanazono University in 2014.
Kenshi Kusano specializes in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University from circa 1971 to 1975 and served as a professor there around 1999.

Kenta Suzuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (circa 1994–1998) and the University of Tokyo (circa 1999–2004). He served as an associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College around 2011 to 2018.

Kenyu Mitomo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Rissho University and UC Berkeley. From 1968 to 2015, he was Dean of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University, and held visiting professorships at Berkeley and Chung-Hwa Institute.

Kevin Alan Vose is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Bates College and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins in 1997, and studied under Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa.

Kevin Buckelew specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Sarah Lawrence College and pursued doctoral studies supervised by Chün-fang Yü, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang, also studying under Yan Ling, Fumiko Nazikian, and Courtney Bender.

Khakyab Dorje was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Khenchen Tashi Özer, Tsuklak Nyinjé, Mingyur Wanggyel, and Sheja Künkhyen, and taught numerous students including Kalu Rinpoche.
Kham Sum Zilnön Gyepa Dorjé studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga. He later taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Khammai Dhammasami is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford (circa 2000–2004). He has served as a professor at ITBMU, an Oxford Buddhist chaplain, and a fellow and trustee at the OCBS.
Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued his traditional education under teachers Jampal Gyepe Dorje and Lodro Gyatso.
Khen Gen Jampal Dorjé was a scholar who studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga.
Khenchen Ngawang Khyen Rab Gyatso studied under the teachers Dilgo Khyentse and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Gochen and Riwoche monasteries under Dudjom Rinpoche and others. From circa 1967 to 1984, he chaired the Nyingma section at CIHTS.
Khenchen Tashi Özer studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He later taught Shechen Gyaltsab and Khakyab Dorje.

Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied under Khenpo Gangshar and the 16th Karmapa. He served as abbot of Rumtek Monastery (circa 1967), Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (circa 1981), and Gampo Abbey.
Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin was a scholar who studied under Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Khenpo Shenga.

Khenpo Appey was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dzongsar Monastery under Drakgyab Lodrö, held a post at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, and served as Director of Sakya College from 1972 to 1985.
Khenpo Dazer was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima. He served as a teacher at both the Shri Singha Shedra and the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute.

Khenpo Gangshar was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Shechen Monastery under Khyentse Ozer, Shyé Chen Kong Trul Pema Drimé, and Karsé Kongtrul. He served as a senior teacher at Shechen Monastery.
